analysis.investment_thesis: Maharashtra Scooters is a passive holding company — a Bajaj group investment vehicle trading at a 55% discount to book (P/B 0.45) — not an operating business riding India's growth story. With revenue declining -1.9% CAGR, EBITDA contracting -9.6% CAGR, and ROE of just 0.69%, this is not the kind of compounding machine I seek.
key_strengths: Deep NAV discount: P/B of 0.45 means market cap (₹15,007 Cr) is less than half of total equity (₹30,863 Cr)
Zero debt: near-clean balance sheet with virtually no leverage
Bajaj group parentage: strong promoter pedigree, 51% holding, consistent dividend payouts (₹193 Cr financing outflow FY25)
key_risks: Conglomerate discount is structural and may persist indefinitely — NAV discounts in Indian holding cos rarely close
Declining operating performance: revenue at ₹183 Cr in FY25 vs ₹222 Cr in FY24, EBITDA down from ₹204 Cr to ₹128 Cr — alarming deterioration
P/E of 41.8x for a holding company with -1.9% revenue CAGR is unjustifiably expensive by any value or growth metric
red_flags: ROE of 0.69% and ROCE of 0.55% — capital is being destroyed in real terms relative to cost of equity
Not an operating business — it is a pure investment vehicle with no exposure to India's consumption/urbanization boom
P/S of 47.87x: investors are paying ₹48 for every rupee of revenue — pricing in value that may never be unlocked
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Maharashtra Scooters is not a scooter company — it is a Bajaj group holding entity that invests in securities and earns dividend/investment income. Its ₹30,863 Cr equity base (largely mark-to-market portfolio, predominantly Bajaj Auto) dwarfs its ₹183 Cr of revenue. The FY25 net profit of ₹214 Cr (+14.5% CAGR) looks fine on paper, but this growth is investment-gain driven — EBITDA collapsed from ₹204 Cr to ₹128 Cr in the same year, signaling the underlying income stream is weak and lumpy. This is not the kind of business where I can model 15-25% earnings compounding with confidence.

From my framework, I need businesses that grow with India — consumer, infrastructure, financial services that deploy capital, pharma. Maharashtra Scooters is a pass-through vehicle where the real alpha lives in the underlying Bajaj portfolio, not in the holding company itself. The 55% NAV discount is tempting, but Indian holding company discounts are notoriously sticky — HDFC Ltd. traded at discounts for decades. At 41.8x P/E with declining revenues and sub-1% ROE, even the NAV discount argument falls flat. I would rather own Bajaj Auto or Bajaj Finance directly at fair value than pay for a holding company structure that adds no value.
